\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ویترین} (vitrin)}{ویترین (vitrin)}]{\fa{ویترین} (vitrin) — a shop window; a display case}

\label{lesson:FA-C460-vitrin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fake, then the Persian for a guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ویترین}}
\textbf{\fa{ویترین}} (\emph{vitrin}) — \textquotedblleft{}a shop window; a display case\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دختر} \fa{جلوی} \fa{ویترین} \fa{ایستاد} \fa{و} \fa{کفشها} \fa{را} \fa{نگاه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dokhtar jolow-ye vitrin istâd va kafsh-hâ râ negâh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl stopped in front of the shop window and looked at the shoes.
\end{quote}

Also a glass cabinet at home for the best china.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vitrin} was borrowed from French \emph{vitrine} 'shop window', which EtymDB derives from \emph{vitre} 'pane of glass'; that goes back to Latin \emph{vitrum} 'glass' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vitrin}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vitrin}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vitrin}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for fake, then the Persian for a guarantee, then say \emph{vitrin} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پاساژ} (pâsâzh)}{پاساژ (pâsâzh)}]{\fa{پاساژ} (pâsâzh) — a shopping arcade, a mall}

\label{lesson:FA-C460-pasazh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a guarantee, then the Persian for a shop window.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پاساژ}}
\textbf{\fa{پاساژ}} (\emph{pâsâzh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a shopping arcade, a mall\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{پاساژ} \fa{یک} \fa{کافه} \fa{کوچک} \fa{هست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar pâsâzh yek kâfe-ye kuchek hast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a small café in the arcade.
\end{quote}

Iranian towns have many \emph{pâsâzh}, covered buildings full of small shops.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâsâzh} was borrowed from French \emph{passage} (EtymDB), a passage, and in French also a covered arcade of shops.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pâsâzh}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a guarantee, then the Persian for a shop window, then say \emph{pâsâzh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرو} \fa{کردن} (porov kardan)}{پرو کردن (porov kardan)}]{\fa{پرو} \fa{کردن} (porov kardan) — to try on (clothes)}

\label{lesson:FA-C460-porov-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a shop window, then the Persian for a shopping arcade.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرو} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پرو} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{porov kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to try on (clothes)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{خرید} \fa{شلوار} \fa{را} \fa{پرو} \fa{کردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qabl az kharid shalvâr râ porov kardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I tried the trousers on before buying them.
\end{quote}

\emph{porov} 'a fitting' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{porov kardan} is built from \emph{porov} 'a fitting', a loan usually traced to French \emph{preuve} 'proof, trial', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتاق} \fa{پرو} (otâq-e porov)}{اتاق پرو (otâq-e porov)}]{\fa{اتاق} \fa{پرو} (otâq-e porov) — a fitting room, a changing room}

\label{lesson:FA-C460-otaq-e-porov}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a shopping arcade, then the Persian for to try on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتاق} \fa{پرو}}
\textbf{\fa{اتاق} \fa{پرو}} (\emph{otâq-e porov}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fitting room, a changing room\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتاق} \fa{پرو} \fa{شلوغ} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{منتظر} \fa{ماندم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Otâq-e porov sholugh bud va montazer mândam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fitting room was busy and I waited.
\end{quote}

\emph{otâq} 'room' + \emph{porov} 'fitting'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{otâq-e porov} is built from \emph{otâq} 'room', a loan usually traced to Turkic \emph{otaq} 'tent, room', and \emph{porov} 'a fitting', usually traced to French \emph{preuve}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پسندیدن} (pasandidan)}{پسندیدن (pasandidan)}]{\fa{پسندیدن} (pasandidan) — to like, to approve of (a thing)}

\label{lesson:FA-C460-pasandidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to try on, then the Persian for a fitting room.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پسندیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{پسندیدن}} (\emph{pasandidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to like, to approve of (a thing)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{این} \fa{پیراهن} \fa{را} \fa{پسندید} \fa{و} \fa{خرید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdaram in pirâhan râ pasandid va kharid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother liked this shirt and bought it.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{pasand-}: \emph{mipasandam}. \emph{Pasand} — taste, liking.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pasandidan} is inherited and is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{passandīdan} 'to approve'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
